question.text: Under SEBI LODR Regulation 31, what is a listed entity required to file?

answer.text: A statement of dividend distribution among shareholders
A statement showing holding of securities / shareholding pattern of the listed entity
A list of shareholders eligible for bonus issues
KYC compliance records of all security holders

explanation.text: The Logic: The NISM-Series-II-A RTA (Corporate) workbook directly states that Regulation 31 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations requires the listed entity to file a statement showing holding of securities (shareholding pattern) — including the break-up of promoter, public and other categories of holders (NISM-Series-II-A workbook p. 62). Option B reproduces this requirement and is uniquely correct. The Trap: Options A, C and D refer to activities (dividend distribution, bonus eligibility, KYC) that may use shareholding data but are not what Regulation 31 itself requires to be filed. The audit flagged the original framing ("primary purpose of filing the shareholding pattern") as ambiguous because, while market transparency and minimum public shareholding monitoring are reasonable inferences from the broader listing-disclosure regime, the workbook pages checked (pp. 62, 182, 188) do not use the phrase "primary purpose" or state those purposes as the basis of Regulation 31. Note: The original stem asked for the "primary purpose" of the filing — a claim not directly worded in the source. The stem has been narrowed to what Regulation 31 actually REQUIRES to be filed, which the workbook states explicitly on p. 62: a statement showing the shareholding pattern. Option B is the source-tight answer.
